STUFF(s, start, len, rep) -> SUBSTR(s, 1, start-1) || rep || SUBSTR(s, start+len) (T-SQL returns NULL when start is 0 or beyond the string; this version does not)
QUOTENAME: no equivalent
FORMATMESSAGE -> FORMAT (printf-style; %i/%u became %d)
PATINDEX('%b%', x) -> REGEXP_INSTR(x, '(?s)b') (case-sensitive; SQL Server's default collation is not - set case_sensitivity 'lower' to add (?i))
STRING_SPLIT(s, sep) -> UNNEST(SPLIT(s, sep)) AS value (same rows; the order of the values is not guaranteed in either engine unless enable_ordinal / WITH OFFSET is used)
DIFFERENCE(a, b) -> position-by-position SOUNDEX comparison (0-4); T-SQL's algorithm can score differently for some inputs
LIKE '[a-c]%' uses T-SQL character classes, converted to REGEXP_CONTAINS
CHARINDEX/INSTR: SQL Server's default collation finds 'A' in 'abc', BigQuery INSTR is case-sensitive (case_sensitivity 'lower' wraps both sides in LOWER())
DATALENGTH -> BYTE_LENGTH (T-SQL counts 2 bytes per NVARCHAR character, BigQuery counts UTF-8 bytes)

string column Name is compared with a text literal: SQL Server's default collation is case-insensitive but BigQuery is case-sensitive, so 'NEW' will not match 'new'. Confirm the data's casing is consistent, or set config 'case_sensitivity': 'lower' to wrap both sides in LOWER()
DATEADD on an expression of unknown type: DATE_ADD only accepts DATE - if it is DATETIME/TIMESTAMP use DATETIME_ADD/TIMESTAMP_ADD (or list the column in config 'column_types')
x AT TIME ZONE z -> TIMESTAMP(x, z), assuming x is a DATETIME (wall-clock time in z)
ISDATE(x) -> IF(SAFE_CAST(x AS DATETIME/DATE) IS NOT NULL, 1, 0): only ISO strings count as dates in BigQuery ('Jan 1 2020', '01/02/2020' return 0 here, 1 in T-SQL)

TRY_PARSE(x AS DATE) -> SAFE_CAST: BigQuery only parses ISO formats (YYYY-MM-DD, plain numbers); T-SQL also accepts culture formats ('12/31/2020', '$1,000') - use SAFE.PARSE_DATE('%m/%d/%Y', x) for those
ISNUMERIC(x) -> IF(SAFE_CAST(x AS FLOAT64) IS NOT NULL, 1, 0): T-SQL also returns 1 for '$', ',', '.', '-', '1e5d' ... and 0 for 'NaN'/'inf'; check the inputs you expect
HASHBYTES: use MD5()/SHA256()/SHA512()
CHECKSUM: use FARM_FINGERPRINT()
BINARY_CHECKSUM: use FARM_FINGERPRINT()
RAND(seed): BigQuery RAND() takes no seed, so the value is not repeatable
CROSS APPLY -> CROSS JOIN UNNEST(ARRAY(SELECT AS STRUCT ...)) AS x (correlated; dry-run it - BigQuery rejects correlated subqueries it cannot de-correlate)
OUTER APPLY -> LEFT JOIN UNNEST(ARRAY(SELECT AS STRUCT ...)) AS x (correlated; dry-run it - BigQuery rejects correlated subqueries it cannot de-correlate)

UPDATE ... FROM: BigQuery raises an error if a target row matches more than one source row (T-SQL silently uses one of them) - make sure the joined source is unique on the join key (aggregate it first if needed)
